title: a shape field's key may be optional, `tainted` qualifies a whole shape, and an absent optional field is the throw an absent array key already is
scope:
the two things a shape type could not say — `{name?: T}`, and `tainted {…}` over a shape whose
text-carrying fields all arrived from outside — and what a read of an optional field answers. The
converter that hydrates a shape from `array<mixed>` and the two request members that wrap it are their
own slices; this record is the type surface they are written against.

summary.headline: A shape field can be optional, and that is a different thing from nullable
summary.body:
`{name?: string}` says the key may be absent; `{name: ?string}` says it is present and may hold
null. They accept different values and stay different types. Reading an optional field answers
the declared type, and if the key is absent the read throws, which is exactly what reading a
missing array key already does; `??` and `isset` are the ways to ask without throwing. A whole
shape can be marked `tainted`, which marks every text-carrying field inside it, including nested
ones. `tainted mixed` is not a type, because nothing could be checked through it.
